neighbours.label: a temporal clause that opens a sentence (When / After / Once + its subject), as opposed to 'when' mid-sentence on the - pole
fire: The bell rang twice. When the children heard it, they ran inside.
Fill in the form. After the payment is confirmed, you will get an email.
We waited in the hall. Once the doors opened, everyone rushed in.
He packed his bag. When he reached the station, the train had left.
Preheat the oven. After the butter melts, stir in the flour.
She finished her tea. Once the rain stopped, she walked home.
Save your work. When the update finishes, restart the computer.
The guests sat down. After the speeches ended, dinner was served.
quiet: The bell rang twice and the children ran inside right away.
Fill in the form and you will get an email with the receipt.
We waited in the hall until everyone rushed in at the doors.
He packed his bag, but the train had left the station already.
Preheat the oven and stir the flour into the melted butter.
She finished her tea and walked home in the light rain.
Save your work and restart the computer to finish the update.
The guests sat down and dinner was served after the speeches.

notes: Card: + peaks on 'When', ' After', 'Once he had', ' the' right after a sentence-initial temporal conjunction; the - pole peaks on ' when' x11 in the middle of a sentence. Probe: opening When/After 0.24-0.35, mid-sentence when 0.03. Near misses put the same clause after the main clause.
